known_issues: Some manuscript folio markers are present in the source; they are not included in the spoken English.
Several biblical allusions are present without printed citations; no spoken chapter-and-verse references were added where the Latin source did not provide them.
The phrase “coram vobis” in chapter sixteen appears contextually awkward and may reflect a corrupt reading for “coram nobis”; it was translated as “before our eyes.”
Chapter twenty-six is truncated at “Et quidam”; the English preserves the break as “And some...”
Chapter twenty-three contains several corrupt spellings: “fnales” was translated as “hunger,” reading “fames,” and “lapor” was translated as “labor.”
The abbreviated closing formula in chapter seventeen was expanded according to its evident doxological sense.
Several biblical quotations are given without printed chapter-and-verse references; these were translated as quotations but not supplied with added citations.
Several biblical quotations are given without printed citations; they have been introduced naturally but not assigned spoken references in the translation unless a citation was printed in the source.
Several readings appear corrupt or scribal, and these are explained in the relevant chunk notes.
The fourth sermon is explicitly marked as missing its beginning.
The first sermon is only the end of a sermon for Epiphany.
Several Latin readings are grammatically rough or reflect medieval spelling; where the intended sense is clear, the translation renders that sense and notes significant cases.
The phrase “ibi mater” in chapter seventeen is ambiguous and has been translated literally as “There is our mother.”
Chapter twenty-five is truncated at “Qui uu[…]”; the English preserves the break as “He who...”
The forms “parciamur” and “parciantur” in Chapter 20 are uncertain; they have been interpreted as sharing or setting aside goods for the poor.
In chapter twenty-four, the phrase “bonis bonis operibus insidare debemus” is corrupt or badly transmitted; it was translated according to the likely sense, “devote yourselves to good works.”
In Chapter 21, several corrupt or awkward readings have been translated by evident sense and documented in the relevant notes: “Sanguinem mei,” “Ne cum aliis predicatio,” and “Ideo petro a domino.”
Manuscript folio markers such as “[f. 4v]” are preserved in the Latin transcription but omitted from the English audio translation.
The closing doxological abbreviations “u. s. s.” and “Quod ipse p.” are abbreviated in the Latin; they have been translated according to the evident liturgical sense.
Biblical quotations in this chunk are generally introduced without printed chapter-and-verse references, so no additional spoken citations were inserted beyond the source’s wording.

chunks.speaker: narrator
chunks.latin: [f. 1r] istam tanta veneratione habeamus. Dies iste tribus miraculis ornatur: Christus hodie a iohanne baptizari voluit; Hodie vinum ex aqua fecit; Hodie stella nova, numquam ante visa, que christum eternum lumen significabat, magos perduxit ad presepium ubi christus iacuit. Unde cum summa devotione celebrate diem istam, ut christus, ad cuius laudem hec agitis, ipse vobis retribuat.
chunks.english: Let us keep this day with such deep reverence. This day is adorned by three miracles. Today Christ chose to be baptized by John. Today he made wine from water. Today a new star, never seen before, which signified Christ, the eternal light, led the Magi to the manger where Christ lay. So celebrate this day with the greatest devotion, so that Christ, whose praise you are honoring by these acts, may himself reward you.
chunks.notes: The manuscript folio marker is not spoken in the English.

chunks.speaker: narrator
chunks.latin: Quamvis christus et sanctissima mater eius esset sine peccato, et non subiacerent legibus quibus nos peccatores subiacemus, tamen, ut nos doceret humilitatem, voluit deferri in templum cum oblationibus et mundari ut peccator. Et ei venienti ad templum occurrebat iustus symeon, qui et in ulnas suas eum suscepit, quia responsum accepit a spiritu sancto non visurum se mortem nisi videret dominum christum natum. Propter quod constituit sancta ecclesia ut ea die omnes cum candelis veniamus ad ecclesiam summa devotione, in honore sancte Marie et filii eius, ut illud verum lumen quod christus est accendatur in cordibus nostris. Occurrebat enim ei venienti ad templum viri religiosi et devote femine cum cancandelis, ut illud verum lumen cum lumine susciperet. Unde monemus vos ut diem istum celebretis [f. 1v] elemosinis vestris, devotis orationibus et omnibus bonis operibus, et peccata vestra hodie defleatis. Quod i. p.
chunks.english: Although Christ and his most holy mother were without sin, and were not subject to the laws to which we sinners are subject, nevertheless, to teach us humility, Christ willed to be carried into the temple with offerings and to be purified as though he were a sinner. And as he came to the temple, righteous Simeon met him and took him in his arms, because he had received an answer from the Holy Spirit that he would not see death until he had seen the Lord Christ born. For this reason holy Church established that, on this day, all of us should come to church with candles and with the greatest devotion, in honor of holy Mary and her Son, so that the true light, which is Christ, may be kindled in our hearts. For when Christ came to the temple, religious men and devout women met him with candles, so that they might receive the true light with visible light. Therefore we urge you to celebrate this day with your alms, your devout prayers, and every good work, and today to weep over your sins. May he himself grant this.
chunks.notes: The printed reading is “cancandelis,” evidently for “candelis,” translated as “candles.” The manuscript folio marker is not spoken. The abbreviation “Quod i. p.” is likely “Quod ipse praestet,” translated as “May he himself grant this,” but the abbreviation is uncertain.

chunks.latin: Fratres karissimi. Cum omni tempore ad hoc laborandum esset ut anime vestre consuleretis, specialiter tamen divina dispositio providit fragilitati humane hos xl. dies, ut quidquid per totum annum delinqueretis in his emendaretis. Et isti dies sunt quasi tocius anni. Ipse enim christus nichil precepit nobis quod ipse non prius in se ipso compleret. Ipse enim ieiunavit xl. dies continue, et esurivit et sitivit sicut et nos. Et ideo nos, fratres karissimi, quandoquidem nos per totum annum vivimus ad libitum nostrum, in cibo et potu et in omnibus vanitatibus, vivamus saltim in his diebus modestius et castius, et humiliemus nos coram deo in ieiunio et fletu, et recurramus ad sacerdotes vestros in penitentia et in confessione, et accusemus nos coram ipsis et coram domino, et ipsi simus iudices nostri, si volumus iudicium dei effugere, ut veram indulgentiam a domino consequamur, et sic ad diem resurrectionis cum leticia veniamus. Ipse enim christus instruit nos quid facturi simus ut gratiam eius mereamur. Precepit enim dicens: Frange esurienti panem tuum, et cetera, et habe pacem et caritatem cum proximo tuo, et sic tu
chunks.english: Dearest brothers, although at every time one ought to work at caring for your souls, divine providence has nevertheless made special provision for human weakness with these forty days, so that whatever you have done wrong throughout the whole year, you may correct during them. These days stand, in a way, for the whole year. For Christ himself commanded us nothing that he did not first fulfill in his own person. He fasted for forty continuous days, and he hungered and thirsted just as we do. Therefore, dearest brothers, since throughout the whole year we live as we please, in food and drink and every kind of vanity, let us at least in these days live more modestly and more chastely. Let us humble ourselves before God with fasting and tears. Let us go to your priests in repentance and confession. Let us accuse ourselves before them and before the Lord. And let us become our own judges, if we wish to escape the judgment of God, so that we may obtain true forgiveness from the Lord and come with joy to the day of the Resurrection. Christ himself teaches us what we must do in order to deserve his grace. For he commanded us, saying: “Break your bread for the hungry,” and so on. And have peace and charity with your neighbor, and then you—
chunks.notes: The numeral “xl.” is rendered as “forty.” The quotation “Break your bread for the hungry” echoes Isaiah, but no formal biblical citation is printed in the source. The printed text ends abruptly with “et sic tu,” so the English also breaks off. The printed “et cetera” is rendered as “and so on,” without completing the quotation from memory.

chunks.speaker: announcer
chunks.chapter_title: The Spirit Calls Sinners to Repentance
chunks.latin: IV. [Sermo initio deperdito]
chunks.english: Sermon 4. [A sermon whose beginning is lost]
chunks.notes: The Latin heading states that the beginning of this sermon is missing.

chunks.speaker: narrator
chunks.latin: [f. 2r] domine, intrabit in regnum celorum, sed qui facit voluntatem patris mei. Monet nos dominus, hortatur et instruit per se et per sanctos suos, ut vitam istam, que plena est omnis doloris et laboris, non sic diligamus quasi semper habituri simus. Invitat nos de hac miseria ad celestia gaudia, de hac peregrinatione ad cecestem patriam. Quare tardamus venire ad patrem nostrum, qui nos diligit super omnia que creavit? Amplectitur enim nos omni desiderio; ipse non dat nobis ea que deficiunt, sed que eterna sunt; non dat miseras dignitates huius seculi, sed dat regnum, ut pariter regnemus cum ipso. Clamat et post nos dicens: Venite ad me omnes qui laboratis et honorati estis, et ego reficiam vos, et aput me invenietis requiem animabus vestris. Igitur, fratres karissimi, invocate hodie spiritum sanctum, qui super discipulos domini sicut est hodie apparuit et confortavit eos et docuit eos omnem veritatem, Ut ille vos doceat et dulcescere vobis faciat fidem et veritatem et dilectionem dei et proximi, et regat vos in corpore et anima. Scimus enim verissime: quotienscumque penitet nos peccasse, et deflemus et gemimus peccata nostra, et ad dominum currimus in vera penitentia, tunc spiritus sanctus possidet cor nostrum. Unde [f. 2v] pariter invocate mecum hodie dominum omnipotentem, ut causa matris sue et omnium sanctorum suorum nos participes faciat gratie spiritus sancti, et maneat super nos, et perducat nos in vitam eternam. amen.
chunks.english: —“Lord,” will enter the kingdom of heaven, but only the one who does the will of my Father. The Lord warns us, urges us, and teaches us, both through himself and through his saints, that we should not love this life, which is full of every sorrow and hardship, as though we were going to possess it forever. He calls us from this misery to heavenly joys, from this pilgrimage to our heavenly homeland. Why do we delay in coming to our Father, who loves us more than everything he has created? He embraces us with all desire. He does not give us things that fail, but things that are eternal. He does not give the wretched honors of this world, but a kingdom, so that we may reign together with him. He calls after us, saying: “Come to me, all you who labor and are burdened, and I will refresh you; and with me you will find rest for your souls.” Therefore, dearest brothers, today call upon the Holy Spirit, who appeared over the Lord’s disciples on this very day, strengthened them, and taught them all truth. Ask him to teach you, to make faith, truth, and the love of God and neighbor sweet to you, and to guide you in body and soul. For we know most truly that whenever we regret having sinned, whenever we weep and groan over our sins and run to the Lord in true repentance, then the Holy Spirit takes possession of our heart. Therefore, all together, call with me today upon the almighty Lord: for the sake of his mother and all his saints, may he make us sharers in the grace of the Holy Spirit, may that grace remain upon us, and may he lead us into eternal life. Amen.
chunks.notes: The opening is fragmentary because the beginning of the sermon is lost. The first sentence echoes the Gospel saying, “Not everyone who says to me, ‘Lord, Lord,’ will enter the kingdom of heaven,” but the printed text begins mid-quotation. The printed “cecelestem” appears as “cecestem,” translated as “heavenly.” The printed “honorati estis” is evidently for “onerati estis,” “are burdened,” in the quotation “Come to me, all you who labor and are burdened.” The manuscript folio markers are not spoken.

chunks.speaker: announcer
chunks.chapter_title: John the Baptist and True Devotion
chunks.latin: V. De s. iohanne baptista.
chunks.english: Sermon 5. On Saint John the Baptist.
chunks.notes: The abbreviation “s.” is expanded as “Saint.”

chunks.speaker: narrator
chunks.latin: Fratres karissimi. Scire debetis quia quicquid sanctis impenditur honoris et venerationis, illud impenditur ipsi domino nostro, cui servierunt dum vixerunt. Et sicut nos diligimus quod aliquis servus noster bene tractatur pro nostra dilectione in domo alterius, ita diligit dominus si pro amore eius sanctos suos honoramus et veneramur. Et ideo moneo vos ut diem istum celebretis orationibus vestris et omnibus operibus caritatis quantum possitis. Quando hic statis in ecclesia, debetis vos intime commendare deo cum corpore et anima vestra, et debetis eum rogare ut ipse habeat vos in manibus suis, ne diabolus aliquam potestatem habeat in vobis; et primum debetis orare pro omni ecclesia et pro omnibus fidelibus defunctis, et debetis orare pro inimicis vestris, ut deus eos convertat ad pacem. Et debetis dare elemosynam vestram, et debetis invicem fidem et veritatem servare. Hoc tale festum placet deo. Et debetis hodie [f. 3r] sanctum iohannem rogare ut ipse sit nuntius noster ad omnipotentem dominum, quod ita conservet vos in presenti vita ut eternam vitam acquiratis. Fratres karissimi, vos debetis scire quis iste iohannes fuerit cuius festum hodie celebramus. Iste est ille iohannes qui christum baptizavit. Ille quoque adeo sanctus fuit ut homines qui in illo tempore fuerunt putarent eum esse christum. Sanctus iohannes autem respondens eis quod nec dignus esset ut solveret corrigiam calciamentorum christi. Iste quoque iohannes fuit qui christum venturum in mundum prenuntiavit, qui totum humanum genus deberet redimere. Iste est ille iohannes cui ipse dominus testimonium dat quod inter natos mulierum non surrexit maior .i. sanctior iohanne baptista. Et quamvis tam sanctus esset, tamen segregavit se ab omnibus et moratus est in deserto, et misero aggresti cibo ibi pastus est, et aspero vestitu de pilis camelorum facto induebatur. Et cum tam sanctus homo, qui pene nihil umquam peccavit, ita se afflixisset pro amore, quod de nobis peccatoribus erit qui cottidie peccamus, et tamen cottidie in magnis deliciis simus, et comedimus ad superfluitatem, et bibimus ad ebrietatem?
chunks.english: Dearest brothers, you should know that whatever honor and reverence is shown to the saints is shown to our Lord himself, whom they served while they lived. Just as we are pleased when one of our servants is treated well in someone else’s house out of love for us, so the Lord is pleased if, out of love for him, we honor and venerate his saints. Therefore I urge you to celebrate this day with your prayers and with every work of charity as much as you can. When you stand here in church, you should commend yourselves deeply to God, body and soul. You should ask him to hold you in his hands, so that the devil may have no power over you. First, you should pray for the whole Church and for all the faithful departed. You should also pray for your enemies, that God may turn them toward peace. You should give your alms, and you should keep faith and truth with one another. This is the kind of feast that pleases God. Today you should ask Saint John to be our messenger before the almighty Lord, so that God may preserve you in this present life in such a way that you may gain eternal life. Dearest brothers, you should know who this John was whose feast we celebrate today. He is the John who baptized Christ. He was so holy that the people of his time thought he was the Christ. But Saint John answered them that he was not even worthy to untie the strap of Christ’s sandals. This John also foretold that Christ would come into the world and redeem the whole human race. He is the John about whom the Lord himself gives this testimony: among those born of women, no one greater—that is, no one holier—has arisen than John the Baptist. And although he was so holy, he nevertheless separated himself from everyone and lived in the desert. There he was fed with poor, wild food and wore rough clothing made from camel’s hair. So if such a holy man, who had almost never sinned at all, afflicted himself in this way for love, what will become of us sinners, who sin every day, and yet every day live in great pleasures, eat to excess, and drink to drunkenness?
chunks.notes: The abbreviation “.i.” is expanded as “that is.” The manuscript folio marker is not spoken.

chunks.speaker: announcer
chunks.chapter_title: Peter's Keys and the Ministry of Forgiveness
chunks.latin: VI. Sancti Petri apostoli.
chunks.english: Sermon 6. Of Saint Peter the Apostle.

chunks.speaker: narrator
chunks.latin: Fratres karissimi. Assidue [f. 3v] cogitare debetis quanto labore sancti dei regnum celorum adepti sunt: terrene substantie non parcebant, corpori non parcebant, sed dederunt pro anima sua. Omnia tormenta patiebantur; omnis pena vilis fuit eis propter amorem dei. Vincti sunt, incarcerati sunt, gladio occisi sunt, in cruce suspensi sunt. Sicut sanctus petrus, cuius festum hodie celebramus, cruci suspensus est, quia predicavit verbum dei et dilexit veritatem; et ideo promeruit quod potestatem accepit a domino ut, cuicumque digne querenti celi portam aperiret, aperta esset ei, et cuicumque clauderet, clausa esset ei. Unde pariter omnes invocemus hodie sanctum Petrum, quem dominus principem apostolorum constituit, ut ipse apud dominum veniam peccatorum nostrorum impetret et ianuam celi aperiat. Et sicut ipse corpus suum tradidit pro anima sua, ita debemus et nos mortificare in nobis omnia vitia nostra, scilicet avariciam, luxuriam, superbiam, perfidiam, gulam, ebrietatem, ut his passionibus et hac pugna vitam mereamur eternam. et commonete hodie sanctum petrum, ut memor sit illius misericordie qua dominus misertus est eius cum eum ter negavit. Permisit enim dominus sanctum petrum labi, ut nobis labentibus possit compati, quia nos ei commisit [f. 4r] sicut oves pastori, dicens: Si diligis me, pasce meas; et sicut indulsi tibi, ita et tu indulge eis. Tu ex fragilitate cecidisti; ipse quoque ex fragilitate sepe cadens. Hanc potestatem petri, qui vocantur episcopi, et nos sacerdotes habemus, quamvis simus peccatores. Ut quicumque ex vera penitentia confugerit ad nos, ei peccata dimittimus. Christus dimittit, et nos precones sumus et iudices quod dimissa sunt peccata, et penitentiam penitenti iniungimus, et ita celum aperimus. Rogate quoque eum hodie ut recordetur sancte ecclesie que sibi commissa est, Et pape nostri, ut deus omnipotens eum dignum reddat ad regenda ecclesiam suam. Deinde rogate eum ut recordetur secularis iudicis nostri imperatoris et omnium, ut dominus omnipotens eos tales faciat ut, dum secularia iuste iudicant, celestem mercedem recipiant. Deinde rogate eum pro omnibus fidelibus defunctis, ut celestem patriam eis hodie aperiat. Rogate eum pro vobis ipsis, ut, qui potestatem habet claudere et aperire celum cuicumque cumque voluerit, vincula peccatorum vestrorum solvat et ianuam nobis celi aperiat. Quod ipse prestet.
chunks.english: Dearest brothers, you should constantly think about how much labor the saints of God endured to gain the kingdom of heaven. They did not spare earthly possessions. They did not spare their bodies, but gave them for the sake of their souls. They endured every torture. Every punishment seemed small to them because of the love of God. They were bound, imprisoned, killed by the sword, and hung on the cross. So too Saint Peter, whose feast we celebrate today, was hung on a cross because he preached the word of God and loved the truth. For that reason he earned the privilege of receiving authority from the Lord: if he opened the gate of heaven for anyone who asked worthily, it would be opened for that person; and if he closed it to anyone, it would be closed. Therefore let us all together call upon Saint Peter today, whom the Lord established as prince of the apostles. Let us ask him to obtain from the Lord forgiveness for our sins and to open the gate of heaven. And just as Peter handed over his body for the sake of his soul, so we too must put to death in ourselves all our vices: greed, lust, pride, faithlessness, gluttony, and drunkenness. By enduring these sufferings and this struggle, may we deserve eternal life. Today also remind Saint Peter to remember the mercy with which the Lord had mercy on him when Peter denied him three times. For the Lord allowed Saint Peter to fall so that he could have compassion on us when we fall, because the Lord entrusted us to him as sheep to a shepherd, saying: “If you love me, feed my sheep; and just as I have forgiven you, so you also forgive them. You fell through weakness; each of them also often falls through weakness.” This authority of Peter is held by those who are called bishops, and by us priests as well, even though we are sinners. So whoever flees to us in true repentance, we forgive that person’s sins. Christ forgives; we are heralds and judges declaring that the sins have been forgiven. We assign penance to the penitent, and in this way we open heaven. Today ask Peter also to remember the holy Church entrusted to him, and our pope, so that almighty God may make him worthy to govern his Church. Then ask Peter to remember our secular judge, the emperor, and all rulers, so that almighty God may make them such people that, while they judge earthly matters justly, they may receive a heavenly reward. Then ask him for all the faithful departed, that today he may open the heavenly homeland to them. Ask him for yourselves as well: since he has authority to close and open heaven to whomever he wills, may he loosen the chains of your sins and open for us the gate of heaven. May he himself grant this.
chunks.notes: The manuscript folio markers are not spoken. The quotation “If you love me, feed my sheep” is printed without a biblical citation in the source. The phrase “cuicumque cumque” is awkwardly duplicated in the Latin; it is translated according to the evident sense, “to whomever he wills.”

chunks.speaker: announcer
chunks.chapter_title: Mary’s Assumption and Intercession
chunks.latin: VII. In assumptione s. m.
chunks.english: Sermon 7. On the Assumption of Saint Mary.
chunks.notes: The abbreviation “s. m.” has been expanded as “Saint Mary.”

chunks.speaker: narrator
chunks.latin: Quicumque convenistis hodie in honore sancte Marie matris domini, toto corde invocate [f. 4v] eam ut intercedat pro peccatis vestris. Ipsa est per quam dominus operatus est salutem humano generi. Ipsa est stella maris vel illuminatio tocius mundi. Mundus iste est quasi mare, quia omni tempore movetur magna instabilitate et numquam in eodem statu permanet. Sicut per evam suasione diaboli casus factus est humano generi, sic per mariam angelo nuntiante salus illuxit toto orbi terrarum. Ipsa est singularis spes omnium qui confugiunt ad eam. Ipsa est per qua dominus noster, filius eius, peccata dimittit. Ipsa est que hodie inter choros angelorum in conspectu dei gaudet leticia eterna. Ipsa est que genuit nobis eternum lumen, ipsum christum filium dei, per quem illuminatus est mundus. Ipsa est a quam nos peccatores confugere debemus. Ipsa est magna spes nostra. Unde levate hodie corda vestra ad omnipotentem dominum, ut ipse, pro matre que hodie corpore et anima recepta est in celum, respiciat super nos, et concedat nobis fidem et veritatem et veram penitentiam et vitam eternam. Unde quoque moneo ut cum summa devotione stetis in ecclesia et oretis que vobis necessaria sunt, et peccata deflete vestra, et rogate inducias, ut penitendo peccata vestra diluatis. Quod ipse prestet.
chunks.english:
All of you who have gathered today in honor of Saint Mary, the Mother of the Lord, call on her with your whole heart, so that she may intercede for your sins. Through her, the Lord has worked salvation for the human race. She is the star of the sea and the light of the whole world.

This world is like a sea, because it is always being tossed about by great instability and never remains in the same condition. Just as, through Eve and the devil’s persuasion, the human race fell, so through Mary, when the angel announced the message, salvation shone over the whole world.

She is the unique hope of all who flee to her for help. Through her, our Lord—her Son—forgives sins. Today, among the choirs of angels, in the sight of God, she rejoices with eternal joy. She gave birth for us to the eternal Light, Christ himself, the Son of God, through whom the world has been enlightened. She is the one to whom we sinners ought to run. She is our great hope.

So today lift up your hearts to the almighty Lord. Because of his Mother, who today was received into heaven in body and soul, may he look kindly on us and grant us faith, truth, true repentance, and eternal life.

And I also urge you: stand in church with the greatest devotion. Pray for what you need. Weep over your sins. Ask for time to amend your lives, so that by repentance you may wash away your sins. May he himself grant this.
chunks.notes: The manuscript folio marker has been omitted from the spoken translation. The Latin has several non-classical forms, such as “per qua” for “per quam” and “a quam” where the sense requires “ad quam”; the translation renders the intended sense.

chunks.speaker: announcer
chunks.chapter_title: Conclusion and Commendation to God
chunks.latin: VIII. [Conclusio sermonis]
chunks.english: Sermon 8. [The close of a sermon]
chunks.notes: The bracketed Latin heading is editorial or rubric-like, but it is tied to the numbered section and is therefore rendered as a chapter heading.

chunks.speaker: narrator
chunks.latin: [f. 5r] Modo committo corpus et animam vestram omnipotenti deo, et sancte marie matri eius, et omnibus sanctis eius, quod hic in terris promereamini ut participes fiatis eterne beatitudinis.
chunks.english: Now I commend your body and soul to almighty God, to Saint Mary his Mother, and to all his saints. May you live worthily here on earth, so that you may become sharers in eternal blessedness.
chunks.notes: The manuscript folio marker has been omitted from the spoken translation.

chunks.speaker: announcer
chunks.chapter_title: Mary’s Nativity and True Repentance
chunks.latin: IX. In nativitate sancte marie.
chunks.english: Sermon 9. On the Nativity of Saint Mary.

chunks.speaker: narrator
chunks.latin: Fratres karissimi. Qui hodie convenistis in honore dei et sancte matris eius, sic state in ecclesia, ut non fiat vobis ad dampnationem. Respiciat unusquisque ad cor suum, in quibus peccatis eum accuset, et reprehendat se ipsum, et peccata sua statuat coram se, et fiat iudex peccatorum suorum, et puniat se vera penitentia, quia penitentia pena est. Et quicumque hoc fecerit, securus erit in die iudicii, quia prevenit iudicium, sicut scriptum est: Si vos ipsos iudicaretis, non utique iudicaremini. Adtendite miseram condicionem vestram. Cum merore et maxima amaritudine vita ista finienda est, et omnia huius mundi relinquenda sunt. Non respicit dominus ad divicias, non respicit ad nobilitatem, non ad pulchritudinem; omnia uno fine concluduntur. Sed in celo fit nobilior, dicior et pulchrior qui hic fuit iustior. Terminus huius vite malis est inicium eterni ignis; Bonis inicium eterne exultationis. Mali dampnantur cum diabolo, cui semper servierunt et cuius voluntatem fecerunt. Boni [f. 5v] vero exultant cum celesti rege inenarrabili leticia, et regnant cum angelis et cum omnibus sanctis in secula seculorum. Igitur querite matrem domini hodie adiutricem, rogate eius pietatem, ut hodie pedibus domini nostri provolvatur, ut nos ab eternis penis eripiat et eterna gaudia concedat. Unde iniungo vobis ut quivis vestrum qui hoc persolvere possit pauperem pascat hodie; qui hoc non possit, det unam elemosynam; et cui illa deest, habeat bonam voluntatem. Quod ipse prestet.
chunks.english:
Dearest brothers, you have gathered today in honor of God and of his holy Mother. So stand in church in such a way that your presence here does not become a cause of condemnation for you.

Let each person look into his own heart and see what sins accuse him. Let him rebuke himself. Let him place his sins before his own eyes. Let him become the judge of his own sins, and let him punish himself with true repentance, because repentance is a penalty. Whoever does this will be safe on the day of judgment, because he has already gone ahead and judged himself. As Scripture says, “If you judged yourselves, you would certainly not be judged.”

Think carefully about your unhappy condition. This life must end in sorrow and great bitterness, and everything in this world must be left behind. The Lord does not look at riches. He does not look at noble birth. He does not look at beauty. All these things are brought to the same end. But in heaven, the person who was more righteous here becomes more noble, richer, and more beautiful.

For the wicked, the end of this life is the beginning of eternal fire. For the good, it is the beginning of eternal joy. The wicked are condemned with the devil, whom they have always served and whose will they have done. But the good rejoice with the heavenly King in unspeakable joy, and they reign with the angels and all the saints forever and ever.

So today ask the Mother of the Lord to help you. Appeal to her loving mercy, so that today she may fall at the feet of our Lord and beg him to rescue us from eternal punishments and grant us eternal joys.

Therefore I urge you: whoever among you can do so should feed a poor person today. Whoever cannot do that should give at least one act of charity. And whoever lacks even that should at least have a good will. May he himself grant this.
chunks.notes: The quotation echoes Paul’s first letter to the Corinthians, chapter eleven, verse thirty-one, but no citation is printed in the source. The manuscript folio marker has been omitted from the spoken translation.

chunks.speaker: announcer
chunks.chapter_title: Saint Michael and the Guardian Angels
chunks.latin: X. De sancto Michahele.
chunks.english: Sermon 10. On Saint Michael.
chunks.notes: The spelling “Michahele” is a medieval form of Michael.

chunks.speaker: narrator
chunks.latin: Dicit dominus in evangelio: Nisi conversi fueritis et non efficiamini sicut parvuli, non intrabitis in regnum celorum. Parvulorum puerorum mos est ut sint simplices, sine invidia, sine odio, nec malum pro malo reddant, et si quis eos leserit, statim tradant oblivioni, et per horam arrideant ei qui eos lesit. Quicumque hos pueros imitantur, quantumcumque sint senes, pueri et filii dei vocantur. Illos tales custodiunt sancti angeli die et nocte, et non dant locum malis angelis ut prevaleant. Cum aliquid boni fecerimus, cum ea que iusta sunt diligimus, cum caste et munde vivimus, prevalent boni angeli. Cum vero portamus odium et invidiam in proximum nostrum, cum concupiscimus rem proximi nostri, cum alii auferimus iniuste que sua sunt, tunc diabolus [f. 6r] cum angelis suis prevalet. Et ideo dicitur Michahel pugnare cum diabolo. Unde, fratres karissimi, omni tempore debemus invocare presidia sancti Michahelis et omnium sanctorum angelorum, ut defendant nos ab insidiis diaboli et muniant animas nostras, ne diabolus eas rapiat. Cavete vobis contra maliciosas artes diaboli, qui numquam dormit sed vigilat; et sicut lupus circa gregem vadit insidiando, si aliquam oviculam rapere possit, sic diabolus circuit ut animas nostras rapiat. Igitur, fratres karissimi, festum istud sancti Michahelis omni studio celebrate, date elemosynas in honore eius, estote benigni in invicem, et nolite fugare sanctos angelos a custodia vestra. Rogate hodie sanctum Michahelem, qui habet potestatem super omnes animas, ut animas vestras cum exierint ab hoc corpore representet in paradysum. Quod ipse prestet.
chunks.english:
The Lord says in the Gospel: “Unless you turn and become like little children, you will not enter the kingdom of heaven.”

The way of little children is to be simple, without envy and without hatred. They do not return evil for evil. And if someone hurts them, they quickly forget it, and within the hour they smile again at the person who hurt them.

Whoever imitates such children, no matter how old they may be, are called children and sons of God. The holy angels guard people like that day and night, and they do not give the evil angels room to overcome them.

When we do something good, when we love what is right, when we live chastely and purely, the good angels prevail. But when we carry hatred and envy against our neighbor, when we desire what belongs to our neighbor, when we unjustly take from others what is theirs, then the devil prevails with his angels. That is why Michael is said to fight against the devil.

So, dearest brothers, at all times we ought to call on the protection of Saint Michael and all the holy angels, so that they may defend us from the devil’s traps and guard our souls, lest the devil snatch them away.

Protect yourselves against the devil’s malicious tricks. He never sleeps, but stays awake. As a wolf prowls around a flock, lying in wait to see whether he can seize some little sheep, so the devil prowls around, trying to seize our souls.

Therefore, dearest brothers, celebrate this feast of Saint Michael with full devotion. Give alms in his honor. Be kind to one another. Do not drive the holy angels away from guarding you. Today ask Saint Michael, who has authority over all souls, to present your souls in paradise when they depart from this body. May he himself grant this.
chunks.notes: The Gospel quotation corresponds to the Gospel of Matthew, chapter eighteen, verse three, but the source gives no citation. The printed Latin reads “et non efficiamini,” literally “and do not become,” which contradicts the Gospel sense; the translation follows the evident intended reading, “et efficiamini,” “and become.” The manuscript folio marker has been omitted from the spoken translation.

chunks.speaker: announcer
chunks.chapter_title: All Saints and the Path to Blessedness
chunks.latin: XI. In natale omnium sanctorum.
chunks.english: Sermon 11. On the Feast of All Saints.
chunks.notes: “In natale” refers to the feast day or heavenly birthday of the saints, not their earthly birth.

chunks.speaker: narrator
chunks.latin: Fratres karissimi. Omni die hortatur nos dominus ut convertamur ad ipsum et faciamus eius voluntatem, et promittit nobis premium, regnum celorum. Omni die clamat post nos, filios nos vocat, ad gaudia celestia nos invitat. Nos autem avertimus aures nostras, et plus diligimus mundum istum, ubi nichil certum, nihil proprii possidemus, quam ut illuc perveniamus, ubi cives angelorum et omnium sanctorum erimus. Videtis, fratres, quomodo electos suos, [f. 6v] quorum hodie festum celebramus, remuneravit. Quid leticie, quid delectationis habeant electi dei in celis, humanus sermo explicare non potest, nec cor alicuius percipere potest. Beati sunt illi qui paucos dies mutant pro eterna iocunditate. Qui sunt illi? Hoc sunt illi de quibus ipse dominus dicit in evangelio: Beati misericordes, qui pupillis et viduis et omnibus qui in labore sunt et miseriis auxilium ferunt quantum possunt. Isti tales misericordiam a domino consequentur; et rursum dicit dominus: Beati pacifici, qui pacem diligunt, qui nullum ledunt, qui miseros defendunt, qui suis contenti sunt, qui aliena non rapiunt, qui nullo odio et invidia torquentur. Isti tales eternam pacem consequentur. Et rursum dicit dominus: Beati humiles, qui multas iniurias propter deum paciuntur; et rursum: Beati mundo corde, qui nichil sceleris cogitant, qui nullum malum moliuntur, qui puri sunt ab homicidio, a periurio, ab adulterio, a fornicatione, ab avaricia. Isti filii dei vocantur. Istorum copiosa merces erit in celis. Infelices enim sunt qui paucis his diebus eternam penam in eternum ignem merentur. Qui sunt isti? Hoc sunt superbi, homicide, predones, periuri, perfidi, adulteri, fornicarii, ebriosi. Isti erunt cum diabolo in eterno igne. State, [f. 7r] qui hodie coram deo et omnibus sanctis eius, et videte in cor vestrum eius quibus peccatis vincti sitis, et reddite vos culpabiles deo et sanctis suis eius, et confitemini ei peccata vestra, ut vos clementer ab eis eripiat et ad celestia gaudia perducat. Quod ipse prestet.
chunks.english:
Dearest brothers, every day the Lord urges us to turn back to him and do his will. And he promises us a reward: the kingdom of heaven. Every day he calls after us. He calls us his children. He invites us to the joys of heaven.

But we turn our ears away. We love this world more—this world where we possess nothing secure, nothing truly our own—than we love reaching that place where we will be fellow citizens with the angels and all the saints.

Brothers, you see how God has rewarded his chosen ones, whose feast we celebrate today. What joy, what delight, God’s chosen ones have in heaven—human speech cannot explain it, and no human heart can fully grasp it. Blessed are those who exchange a few short days for eternal gladness.

Who are they? They are the ones of whom the Lord himself says in the Gospel: “Blessed are the merciful.” These are the people who help orphans, widows, and all who are in hardship and misery, as much as they can. People like this will obtain mercy from the Lord.

And again the Lord says: “Blessed are the peacemakers.” These are the people who love peace, who harm no one, who defend the suffering, who are content with what is their own, who do not seize what belongs to others, and who are not tortured by hatred and envy. People like this will obtain eternal peace.

And again the Lord says: “Blessed are the humble,” those who endure many injuries for God’s sake. And again: “Blessed are the pure in heart,” those who plan no wickedness, who plot no evil, who are clean from murder, perjury, adultery, fornication, and greed. These are called children of God. Their reward will be abundant in heaven.

But truly miserable are those who, for the sake of these few short days, earn eternal punishment in eternal fire. Who are they? They are the proud, murderers, robbers, perjurers, the faithless, adulterers, fornicators, and drunkards. They will be with the devil in eternal fire.

So stand today before God and all his saints. Look into your heart, and see by what sins you are bound. Admit your guilt before God and his saints. Confess your sins to him, so that he may mercifully rescue you from them and lead you to the joys of heaven. May he himself grant this.
chunks.notes: The beatitudes quoted here come from the Gospel tradition, especially the Gospel of Matthew, chapter five, but no chapter-and-verse citation is printed. The manuscript folio markers have been omitted from the spoken translation. The Latin in the final exhortation is grammatically rough; the translation gives the evident sense.

chunks.speaker: announcer
chunks.chapter_title: Saint Martin’s Mercy and Charity
chunks.latin: XII. Sancti Martini.
chunks.english: Sermon 12. Of Saint Martin.

chunks.speaker: narrator
chunks.latin: Fratres karissimi. Non est sine causa quod sancta ecclesia sanctorum festivitates per singulos annos celebrat. Ad salutem nostram preordinatum est ut ad eorum patrocinia confugiamus, et quod eorum sanctam conversationem imitemur quantum possimus. Ideo, fratres karissimi, imitamini opera sancti martini, cuius diem hodie celebramus. Videte quante misericordie et quante bonitatis esset, et quantum diligeret deum, qui media hieme, quando frigus durissimum est, cum omnes vestes suas dedisset pauperibus preter pallium unum, quoque illud divisit medium, et unam partem dedit pauperi, aliam reservavit sibi. Unde factum est quod in eadem nocte vidit christum indutum illa dimidia veste qua pauperem vestivit, dicentem sanctis angelis: Martynus adhuc caticuminus, et cetera. Et ideo quicquid tribuitur pauperibus, deo tribuitur. Sicut ipse testatur: Quod uni ex minimis meis fecistis, michi fecistis. Et ex hac magna bonitate promeruit hoc donum a deo accipere, quod quoque tres mortuos resuscitavit. Unde pariter [f. 7v] oremus hodie, ut eius interventu ab eterna morte resuscitemur. Monemus quoque vos, sicut iuste debemus, ut preceptis dei obediatis, et ne despiciatis eius paternas admonitiones, quia semper ad hoc tendit ut conservet nos sicut filios suos eterne hereditatis. Operemur ergo, fratres karissimi, que numquam deficiunt. Que sunt illa opera? fidem et veritatem servemus omnibus proximis nostris. Nulli iniuriam faciamus. Omnibus quibus possumus prodesse debemus; pauperes invitemus in domum nostram. Demus eis vestes, demus eis cibum et potum cibum. Sed cum dominus sit omni die in medio vestri in specie pauperis, oportet ut sepius recipiamus eum, ut et ipse nos suscipiat, cum quo beatus martynus sine fine regnat. Invocate ergo sanctum martynum, ut ipse sit intercessor noster, ut gratiam dei promereri possimus et letari cum ipso in eterna leticia. Quod ipse prestet.
chunks.english:
Dearest brothers, holy Church does not celebrate the feasts of the saints each year without reason. It has been arranged for our salvation that we should flee to their protection and imitate their holy way of life as much as we can.

So, dearest brothers, imitate the works of Saint Martin, whose feast we celebrate today. See how great his mercy and goodness were, and how much he loved God. In the middle of winter, when the cold was extremely harsh, he had already given all his clothes to the poor except one cloak. Then he divided even that cloak in two: one part he gave to a poor man, and the other he kept for himself.

Because of this, that same night he saw Christ clothed in the half-garment with which he had clothed the poor man. Christ was saying to the holy angels, “Martin, still only a catechumen,” and so on.

Therefore, whatever is given to the poor is given to God. As Christ himself testifies: “What you did for one of the least of mine, you did for me.” And because of this great goodness, Martin deserved to receive from God the gift of even raising three dead people to life.

So today let us pray together that, through Martin’s intercession, we may be raised from eternal death. We also warn you, as we rightly ought, to obey God’s commandments and not despise his fatherly warnings, because he is always working for this purpose: to preserve us as his children for the eternal inheritance.

Therefore, dearest brothers, let us do works that never fail. What are those works? Let us keep faith and truth with all our neighbors. Let us do injury to no one. We ought to help everyone we can. Let us invite the poor into our homes. Let us give them clothing, food, and drink.

Since the Lord is among you every day in the form of a poor person, we ought to receive him often, so that he may also receive us—he with whom blessed Martin reigns without end. So call on Saint Martin, that he may be our intercessor, so that we may deserve the grace of God and rejoice with him in eternal joy. May he himself grant this.
chunks.notes: The Latin quotation “Martynus adhuc caticuminus, et cetera” abbreviates the famous scene from the Life of Saint Martin; the translation does not complete the quotation beyond what is printed. The saying “What you did for one of the least of mine, you did for me” echoes the Gospel of Matthew, chapter twenty-five, verse forty, but no citation is printed. The manuscript folio marker has been omitted from the spoken translation. The printed Latin repeats “cibum” at the end of “cibum et potum cibum”; the translation renders the evident sense, “food and drink.”

chunks.speaker: announcer
chunks.chapter_title: Trusting God on Any Feast Day
chunks.latin: XIII. In quocumque festo.
chunks.english: Sermon 13. For any feast.
chunks.notes: The Roman numeral has been standardized to an Arabic chapter number for audio.

chunks.speaker: narrator
chunks.latin: Consulimus vobis, fratres karissimi, ut deum diligatis ex omni cogitatione, ex toto corde, et quod committatis ei corpus et animam vestram, et ubicumque possitis voluntatem eius faciatis, quia sine gratia eius nichil facere potestis. In illius manus committite vos, et habete eum coram oculis [f. 8r] vestris, et rogate eum ut emolliat cor vestrum, ut peccata vestra deflere possitis, quia nemo est qui adiuvare nos possit si ipse non adiuvet nos. Nullus speret in divitiis suis, nullus in thesauris suis. Nullus in magnis castellis suis, nullus in lato fundo. Hec omnia non prosunt illi qui deum offendit. Hec omnia aufert deus quando vult, Sicut vos sepe vidistis quomodo principes potentes humiliati sunt, Quomodo captivati sunt, Quomodo incarcerati sunt. Vidistis multos divites ad maximam miseriam redactos. Quando deum offendimus, tunc nusquam oportet nos esse securos. Multis modis ostendit nobis dominus quod hec omnia que in mundo sunt incerta et caduca sunt. Ideo rogamus et monemus vos ut causa anime vestre convertamini ad deum vestrum, nec decipiat vos mundus iste, qui est plenus omni labore et dolore. Sed tamen nullus est iam inter divites et pauperes qui aliud intendat in hoc mundo quam ut dicior fiat et multa colligat, sed nescit cui relinquat et quando relinquat. Consulimus ergo vobis in caritate omnipotentis dei ut verba que hodie diximus vobis in corde vestro retineatis, ut ibi radicent et bonum fructum afferant. Committo vos hodie gratie sancti spiritus, ut ille immittat cordi vestro bonam [f. 8v] voluntatem et bona opera. Quod ipse prestet.
chunks.english:
Dearest brothers, we urge you to love God with your whole mind and your whole heart. Entrust your body and your soul to him, and wherever you can, do his will, because without his grace you can do nothing.

Place yourselves in his hands. Keep him before your eyes. Ask him to soften your heart, so that you may be able to weep over your sins, because no one can help us unless he helps us.

Let no one put hope in wealth, or in treasure, or in great castles, or in broad estates. None of these things helps the person who has offended God. God takes them all away whenever he wills. You yourselves have often seen powerful rulers humbled, taken captive, and thrown into prison. You have seen many rich people reduced to extreme poverty. When we offend God, then nowhere should we think ourselves safe.

In many ways the Lord shows us that everything in this world is uncertain and passing away. So we ask you and warn you: for the sake of your soul, turn back to your God. Do not let this world deceive you, for it is full of toil and sorrow.

And yet now, among rich and poor alike, hardly anyone in this world aims at anything except becoming richer and piling up possessions—though he does not know to whom he will leave them, or when he will have to leave them behind.

So, in the love of almighty God, we urge you: keep in your heart the words we have spoken to you today, so that they may take root there and bear good fruit. Today I entrust you to the grace of the Holy Spirit. May he put good will and good works into your heart. May he himself grant this.
chunks.notes: Manuscript folio markers have been omitted from the English, as editorial or codicological apparatus.

chunks.speaker: announcer
chunks.chapter_title: Sending Good Works Ahead to Heaven
chunks.latin: XIV. Item in quolibet festo.
chunks.english: Sermon 14. Likewise, for any feast.
chunks.notes: The Latin heading means “Again, for any feast.” The chapter title summarizes the main exhortation that follows.

chunks.speaker: narrator
chunks.latin: Velimus nolumus, transeundum nobis est ab hoc mundo. Ideo beati sunt illi qui aliquid boni premittunt unde eternaliter vivant. Mirum est, fratres karissimi: nos solliciti sumus unde paucos annos hic vivamus, non cogitamus unde eternaliter vivere debeamus. Vere dico vobis quia nichil ibi invenitur nisi hinc premittatur. Tendite, fratres karissimi, ad patriam vestram. Ipse invitat vos et hortatur exire de hac peregrinatione. Nolite esse desides; maiora ibi inveniuntur quam ab aliquo premitti possint. Nullus ibi labor est, nullus dolor. Ibi nichil est nisi gaudium et leticia in presentia dei. Ibi est exultatio cum angelis et omnibus sanctis eius. Unde rogate qui diligit nos super omnem creaturam suam, ut ipse dignetur nobis porrigere manum suam, ut eripiat nos de erumpnis huius seculi. Quod ipse prestet.
chunks.english:
Whether we want to or not, we must pass out of this world. Blessed, then, are those who send some good ahead of them, so that they may live forever.

It is strange, dearest brothers: we worry about how we will live here for a few years, but we do not think about how we ought to live forever. Truly I tell you, nothing will be found there unless it has been sent ahead from here.

So press on, dearest brothers, toward your homeland. The Lord himself invites you and urges you to leave this pilgrimage behind. Do not be lazy. Greater things are found there than anyone could possibly send ahead. There is no labor there, no sorrow. There is nothing there but joy and gladness in the presence of God. There is rejoicing with the angels and with all his saints.

So pray to the one who loves us above every creature of his. Ask him to stretch out his hand to us and rescue us from the miseries of this age. May he himself grant this.

chunks.speaker: announcer
chunks.chapter_title: Hope for Sinners through Repentance
chunks.latin: XV. Alius sermo.
chunks.english: Sermon 15. Another sermon.
chunks.notes: The Latin heading simply says “Another sermon.” The descriptive title is drawn from the sermon’s repeated theme.

chunks.speaker: narrator
chunks.latin: Fratres karissimi, apostolus dicit: Omnes peccavimus et egemus gloria dei. Omnes peccatores sumus, sed misericordia dei maior est quam peccata nostra. Nullum terreant peccata sua quantumcumque sint magna; tantum convertatur et penitentiam agat, et salvus erit. Sic enim scriptum est: Peccasti, quiesce. deus non spernit peccatores, sed penitere nolentes. Si quis adulter est, si quis [f. 9r] fornicator, si quis homicida, si quis periurus, si quis fenerator, si quis aliis sceleribus circumdatus, non desperet, quia pro his venit dominus in hunc mundum ut hos salvaret. Sicut ipse dicit: Non veni vocare iustos, sed peccatores. et videte que exempla proposuisset nobis. Latro in cruce, cum deberet mori, penituit quod fecit et dixit: Domine, miserere mei dum veneris in regnum tuum. Et respondit ei dominus: Vere dico tibi quia hodie mecum eris in paradiso. Et per hoc dedit nobis magnam spem, latronibus et peccatoribus et aliis sceleratis, quod latro post veram penitentiam priusquam aliquis sanctorum adscendit ad gloriam. David reus erat adulterii et homicidii, et penituit eum quod fecit, et dictum est ei a propheta domini nathan: dimissum est peccatum tuum. et per hoc dedit dominus magnam spem omnibus qui adulterii et homicidii rei sunt. Maria peccatrix universis viciis plena erat, et venit cum vera penitentia et multis lacrimis ad pedes domini et deosculabatur eos, donec dimisit ei omnia peccata sua; et tantum honoravit eam quod ei primum post resurrectionem suam apparuit, et apostolis resurrectionem nuntiavit; et per hoc magnam spem dedit omnibus viris et mulieribus qui ex fragilitate sua lapsi sunt. Zacheus publicanus, qui multos defraudaverat, ex [f. 9v] vera penitentia quadrupliciter omnia restituit, et per hoc promeruit christum in domum suam recipere. Et per hoc dedit dominus magnam spem mercatoribus qui cum fraude emunt vel vendunt. Nam vera penitentia est verum remedium contra omnia peccata. Matheus thelonearius multis bona sua iniuste extorserat, et per veram penitentiam factus est apostolus et evangelista. Petrus negavit dominum, et vera penitentia et lacrimis promeruit quod factus est princeps apostolorum. Hec omnia magnam spem dant nobis peccatoribus. Et dico vobis quod gaudium fit angelis dei super conversione unius peccatoris. Igitur nullus peccator desperet. Quacumque enim die conversus fuerit ad dominum, quoque si multis criminibus cecidisset, cum gaudio suscipietur. Semper clamat post nos ut revertamur ad ipsum. Qui vere penitens est securus erit de peccatis suis. Sed quicumque vestrum adhuc veram penitentiam non habet, roget deum et pulset ad ianuam divine clementie, et aperietur ei et dabitur ei quod petit. Unde rogamus et monemus vos ut omni tempore deum coram oculis vestris habeatis, qui omnia dedit nobis que habemus et adhuc regnum celorum promittit. Ad quod vos perducat qui sine fine vivit et regnat.
chunks.english:
Dearest brothers, the Apostle says, “We have all sinned and lack the glory of God.” We are all sinners, but God’s mercy is greater than our sins. Let no one be terrified by his sins, however great they may be. Let him only turn back, do penance, and he will be saved.

For Scripture says, “You have sinned; now stop.” God does not reject sinners. He rejects those who refuse to repent.

If someone is an adulterer, or sexually immoral, or a murderer, or perjured, or a usurer, or caught in other crimes, he should not despair. The Lord came into this world for such people, to save them. As he himself says, “I did not come to call the righteous, but sinners.”

Look at the examples he has set before us. The thief on the cross, when he was about to die, repented of what he had done and said, “Lord, have mercy on me when you come into your kingdom.” And the Lord answered him, “Truly I tell you, today you will be with me in paradise.” In this way the Lord gave great hope to us, to thieves, sinners, and other wrongdoers: after true repentance, the thief entered glory before any of the saints.

David was guilty of adultery and murder. He repented of what he had done, and the Lord’s prophet Nathan said to him, “Your sin has been forgiven.” In this way the Lord gave great hope to all who are guilty of adultery and murder.

Mary was a sinful woman, full of every vice. She came with true repentance and many tears to the Lord’s feet and kissed them, until he forgave her all her sins. He honored her so greatly that after his resurrection he appeared first to her, and she announced the resurrection to the apostles. In this way he gave great hope to all men and women who have fallen because of human weakness.

Zacchaeus the tax collector had cheated many people. But through true repentance he restored everything fourfold, and so he was found worthy to receive Christ into his house. In this way the Lord gave great hope to merchants who buy or sell fraudulently.

True repentance is the real remedy against every sin. Matthew the tax collector had unjustly extorted goods from many people, but through true repentance he became an apostle and an evangelist. Peter denied the Lord, but through true repentance and tears he deserved to become the leader of the apostles.

All these things give great hope to us sinners. And I tell you: there is joy among God’s angels over the conversion of one sinner. Therefore let no sinner despair. On whatever day he turns back to the Lord, even if he has fallen into many crimes, he will be received with joy. The Lord is always calling after us to return to him.

Whoever is truly repentant may be confident about his sins being forgiven. But if any of you does not yet have true repentance, let him ask God and knock at the door of divine mercy. It will be opened to him, and he will be given what he asks.

So we ask you and warn you: keep God before your eyes at all times. He has given us everything we have, and he still promises us the kingdom of heaven. May the one who lives and reigns without end lead you there.
chunks.notes: The sermon quotes or echoes several biblical passages without printed chapter-and-verse references. Following the standardization rule, no added citation has been spoken where the source gives none. The statement that Mary was the first witness of the resurrection reflects the preacher’s traditional identification of Mary Magdalene with the repentant sinful woman.

chunks.speaker: announcer
chunks.chapter_title: Fleeing a Collapsing World
chunks.latin: XVI. Alius.
chunks.english: Sermon 16. Another.
chunks.notes: The Latin heading simply says “Another.” The descriptive title reflects the sermon’s apocalyptic warning and call to repentance.

chunks.speaker: narrator
chunks.latin: [f. 10r] Fratres karissimi. Tempora novissima et periculosa instant. Fides et veritas et omnis iusticia defecerunt. Non invenitur iam fides inter servum et dominum, inter virum et uxorem. Et omnis iniquitas et vanitas adeo iam invaluit quod ira dei et plaga eius merito venit super nos. Videmus famem coram vobis. Videmus sterilitatem frumenti et vini. Videmus predas et incendia per totam terram. Videmus quod gens contra gentem surgit. Videmus romanum imperium destrui. Deinde et leges humane penitus defecerunt. Mundus iam casum minatur. Fugiamus ergo ne obruamur cum mundo. Si quis maneret in domo sua que ex vetustate nutaret, nonne cicius inde exiret ut ad loca tuciora fugeret? Fugiamus de hoc mundo et de hoc exilio ad patriam nostram que in celis est, ad quam ipse pater noster, qui nobis dedit corpus et animam, invitat nos sic dicens: Venite benedicti patris mei. Moneo ergo et exhortor vos pro meo officio ut unusquisque conscientiam suam interroget quibus peccatis suis dominum offenderit, et confiteatur deo et sacertoti suo, et iudicet se ipsum, si vult futurum iudicium dei. Sicut dicit apostolus: Si vos ipsos iudicaretis, non utique iudicaremini. Adtendite, fratres karissimi. Vita nobis brevis et incerta est: ut flos qui hodie floret et cras arescet et cadet, sic vita nostra deficit. [f. 10v] Igitur vigilate omni tempore in elemosynis, ieiuniis, orationibus, omnibus bonis operibus, quia nescitis diem quando dies domini ut fur in nocte veniat et separat corpus ab anima, et ultra locus non erit penitentie; tunc ibimus illuc quo meruimus, sive ad eternam requiem sive ad eternum ignem. Preparate vobis locum in celo, ubi pax et leticia est sine fine, et tale gaudium quod nec oculus vidit nec in cor hominis ascendit, quod preparavit deus diligentibus se. Ad hoc gaudium vos perducat qui sine fine vivit et regnat.
chunks.english:
Dearest brothers, the last and dangerous times are pressing in. Faith, truth, and all justice have failed. Faithfulness is hardly found anymore between servant and master, or between husband and wife. Every kind of injustice and emptiness has now grown so strong that God’s anger and his scourge rightly come upon us.

We see famine before you. We see a failure of grain and wine. We see plundering and fires throughout the whole land. We see nation rising against nation. We see the Roman Empire being destroyed. And beyond that, human laws have utterly failed. The world is already threatening to collapse.

So let us flee, so that we are not buried under the world when it falls. If someone were staying in a house that was shaking from age, would he not leave it at once and flee to safer places? Let us flee from this world and from this exile to our homeland in heaven. Our Father himself, who gave us body and soul, invites us there when he says, “Come, blessed ones of my Father.”

Therefore, as part of my office, I warn you and urge you: let each person question his own conscience, asking by which sins he has offended the Lord. Let him confess to God and to his priest. Let him judge himself, if he wishes to avoid God’s future judgment. As the Apostle says, “If you judged yourselves, you would certainly not be judged.”

Pay attention, dearest brothers. Life is short and uncertain for us. Just as a flower blooms today and tomorrow dries up and falls, so our life fades away.

Therefore keep watch at all times with almsgiving, fasting, prayer, and every good work. You do not know the day when the day of the Lord will come like a thief in the night and separate body from soul. After that, there will be no place left for repentance. Then we will go where we have deserved to go: either to eternal rest or to eternal fire.

Prepare a place for yourselves in heaven, where there is peace and gladness without end, and a joy like the one Scripture describes: “No eye has seen, nor has it entered into the human heart, what God has prepared for those who love him.” May the one who lives and reigns without end lead you to that joy.
chunks.notes: The phrase “coram vobis,” literally “before you,” is awkward in context; I translated the evident sense, “before our eyes.” The printed text gives no chapter-and-verse references for the biblical quotations.  The Latin 'si vult futurum iudicium dei' has no infinitive (literally 'if he wishes God's future judgment'); 'to avoid' is supplied from the sense (reviewer r02-02; transcription normalizer flagged the same clause).

chunks.speaker: announcer
chunks.chapter_title: Preparing the Soul for Death
chunks.latin: XVII. Alius.
chunks.english: Sermon 17. Another.
chunks.notes: The Latin heading simply says “Another.” The descriptive title is drawn from the sermon’s central exhortation.

chunks.speaker: narrator
chunks.latin: Fratres karissimi. Moneo vos et hortor ut anime vestre consulatis, que eternaliter permanebit, sive in celo sive in inferno. Operamini ergo omne opus bonum dum tempus habetis, quia totum spatium huius vite datum est nobis in spacium penitentie, quia post mortem omnis penitentia infructuosa erit. Preparate itaque vos ad diem mortis; ornate vos humilitate, castitate, continentia, caritate. Hec sunt vestes albe que placent in conspectu regis summi. Laborate hinc exire, laborate exire de medio iniquitatis, de tenebris huius mundi, ad terram repromissionis: ibi nos expectat angelorum chorus, ibi prophetarum numerus, ibi omnes sancti occurrunt, ibi mater, ibi omnis cognatio nostra leta. Nonne quivis nostrum, cum iturus est in curiam vel in [f. 11r] alium locum ubi multi congregantur, ornat se vestibus candidioribus, componit capillos, ne aliquid sit unde oculos multorum offendat? Quanto magis, cum ituri sumus in conspectu domini nostri, ornari debemus bonis operibus. Quod u. p. d. qui cum p. s. s. vivit et regnat.
chunks.english:
Dearest brothers, I warn you and urge you: take thought for your soul. It will remain forever, either in heaven or in hell.

So do every good work while you have time, because the whole span of this life has been given to us as a time for repentance. After death, every act of repentance will be fruitless.

Therefore prepare yourselves for the day of death. Clothe yourselves with humility, chastity, self-control, and love. These are the white garments that are pleasing in the sight of the highest King.

Strive to leave this place. Strive to come out from the midst of injustice, from the darkness of this world, into the promised land. There the choir of angels awaits us. There is the company of prophets. There all the saints come to meet us. There is our mother. There all our family rejoices.

When any one of us is about to go to court, or to some other place where many people gather, does he not dress himself in brighter clothing and arrange his hair, so that there will be nothing to offend the eyes of the crowd? How much more, when we are about to go into the presence of our Lord, should we be adorned with good works.

May he be pleased to grant this to you, he who with the Father and the Holy Spirit lives and reigns.
chunks.notes: The final doxology is heavily abbreviated in the printed Latin: “Quod u. p. d. qui cum p. s. s. vivit et regnat.” I expanded it according to the evident liturgical sense. “There is our mother” is ambiguous; it may refer to Mary, the Church, or one’s redeemed kin. I left the ambiguity in the translation.

chunks.speaker: announcer
chunks.chapter_title: The Poor Are Comforted by Hope in God
chunks.latin: XVIII. Alius.
chunks.english: Sermon 18. Another.
chunks.notes: The Latin heading, “Alius,” means “Another,” that is, another sermon or admonition. A descriptive title has been supplied from the content.

chunks.speaker: narrator
chunks.latin: Vos qui pauperes estis, qui substantia huius mundi caretis, deus consololabitur vos si in ipso sperabitis, et si cum pacientia paupertatem vestram subportare vultis. Omnem spem vestram ponite in eo, quoniam ipsi cura est de vobis, et apud eum sunt divicie que manent in eternum. Christus non promisit electis suis divicias huius mundi, sed laborem et dolorem in hoc seculo. Sicut ipse dicit: Mundus gaudebit, vos autem contristabimini, sed tristicia vestra vertetur in gaudium; quando mecum regnabitis, in eterna leticia gaudebitis. Monemus vos ut vestras divitias comportetis in celum, ubi fur non effodiet, ubi latro non aufert, ubi nullus potentior a vobis extorquet. Et sicut in substantia pauperes estis, ita et in concupiscentia pauperes estote, ita ut nichil aliud queratis, nichil aliud concupiscatis, nisi quod deus ex sua gratia vobis obtulerit. Et scitote quia nichil deerit timentibus deum. Multi enim divicias huius mundi ad dampnationem anime sue habent, quia ex eis superbi sunt, pauperiores contempnunt, pauperes depredantur, nullam reverentiam deo exhibent, omnia ad libitum suum faciunt. Pauperes autem, qui famem paciuntur, sitim et frigus, sepius confugiunt ad deum, qui restringit eos laboribus huius mundi ne dulcescat eis iste mundus, ut facilius eos ad se, dum nichil habeant in hoc mundo quod eos delectet. Ideo convertimini ad eum ex toto corde, et ipse erit consolatio paupertatis vestre. Qui vivit et regnat u. s. s.
chunks.english:
You who are poor, you who lack the possessions of this world: God will comfort you, if you put your hope in him and are willing to bear your poverty with patience. Place all your hope in him, because he cares for you, and with him are riches that remain forever.

Christ did not promise the riches of this world to his chosen ones, but labor and sorrow in this present age. As he himself says, “The world will rejoice, but you will grieve; yet your grief will be turned into joy.” And when you reign with me, you will rejoice in eternal gladness.

So we urge you: carry your riches into heaven. There no thief breaks in, no robber takes them away, and no one more powerful can extort them from you. And just as you are poor in possessions, be poor also in desire. Seek nothing else, desire nothing else, except what God, by his grace, has offered you. And know this: those who fear God will lack nothing.

Many people possess the riches of this world to the condemnation of their own souls. Because of those riches they become proud, despise those who are poorer, plunder the poor, show no reverence to God, and do everything according to their own pleasure.

But the poor, who suffer hunger, thirst, and cold, more often flee for refuge to God. He restrains them through the hardships of this world, so that this world may not become sweet to them, and so that, having nothing in this world to delight them, they may more easily be drawn to him.

Therefore turn to him with your whole heart, and he will be the comfort of your poverty. He lives and reigns forever.
chunks.notes: “Consololabitur” is a corrupt spelling for “consolabitur,” translated as “will comfort.” The quotation echoes the Gospel of John, chapter sixteen, verse twenty, though no reference is printed in the source. The closing abbreviation “u. s. s.” appears to mean “ut supra” or a similar reference to the standard doxology; it is rendered in sense as a brief blessing.

chunks.speaker: announcer
chunks.chapter_title: Priests Must Guard the Souls Entrusted to Them
chunks.latin: XIX. Alius.
chunks.english: Sermon 19. Another.
chunks.notes: The Latin heading, “Alius,” means “Another.” A descriptive title has been supplied from the content.

chunks.speaker: narrator
chunks.latin: Necesse est, fratres karissimi, ut sepius moneamus vos, quia sumus sacerdotes vestri et rationem reddituri sumus de anima vestra, si diabolus, ille lupus invisibilis, aliquam rapuerit. Et sicut respondere debet pastor de perdita ove, sic sacerdos de perdita anima. Ideo monemus vos et rogamus ut fide et veritatem invicem conservetis; nullus alii fraudem faciat; quod sibi non vult, alii non faciat. Diligite deum qui vos diligit. Diligite patrem vestrum qui vobis animam et corpus dedit; habete eum in corde vestro. Videte que sit voluntas eius, et hoc facite. Omnis voluntas eius et cogitatio hec est, ut conservet vos. O quanta dignitas, quod ipse nos filios vocat. Vere illi soli beati sunt qui deum diligunt, et qui adherent ei, et qui invocant nomen eius, et bona opera operantur. Ecce, ut dilectionem quam habuit in nos manifestaret, se ipsum dedit pro peccatis suis. Nos peccavimus, et ipse peccata nostra luit.
chunks.english:
It is necessary, dearest brothers, that we admonish you often, because we are your priests, and we will have to give an account for your souls if the devil, that invisible wolf, snatches any one of them away. Just as a shepherd must answer for a lost sheep, so a priest must answer for a lost soul.

Therefore we admonish you and beg you: preserve faith and truth among yourselves. Let no one defraud another. What you do not want done to yourself, do not do to someone else.

Love God, who loves you. Love your Father, who gave you soul and body. Keep him in your heart. Consider what his will is, and do that. His whole will and purpose is this: to preserve you.

Oh, what great dignity it is that he calls us his children! Truly, only those are blessed who love God, cling to him, call upon his name, and do good works.

Look: to make clear the love he had for us, he gave himself for our sins. We sinned, and he paid the debt for our sins.
chunks.notes: The printed Latin says “se ipsum dedit pro peccatis suis,” literally “he gave himself for his own sins,” but the context and theology require “for our sins”; translated accordingly. “Luit” means he paid, expiated, or discharged the penalty.

chunks.speaker: announcer
chunks.chapter_title: Sharing the Harvest in the Common Week
chunks.latin: XX. Sermo in ebdomada que dicitur communis.
chunks.english: Sermon 20. Sermon in the week that is called the Common Week.
chunks.notes: “Ebdomada que dicitur communis” is rendered as “the Common Week,” meaning a week of shared observance and almsgiving.

chunks.speaker: narrator
chunks.latin: Predicare debemus vobis quare ecclesia consuesit hanc ebdomadam plus quam alias in anno maiori observatione elemosinarum celebrare. Sic constituerunt sancti qui ante nos fuerunt, et parentes nostri, viri sancti, qui deum ex toto corde diligebant. Bonum visum est eis ut post collectionem frugum tunc de his pauperibus parciamur in memoriam vivorum et defunctorum et parentum nostrorum, et ad laudem dei et gloriam dei, qui nobis ea contulit. Et ideo dicitur vulgo communis ebdomada, ut omnes communiter celebrent hanc ebdomadam omnibus bonis operibus, quisque pro sua copia, ut deus ea que dedit conservet et custodiat ab igne, a latronibus, ab omni mala incursione. Illi quibus dedit deus substantiam huius mundi parciantur his qui non habent. Quia cui deus plus contulit, plus exigit ab eo. Pauperiores autem orent deum pro divitibus, ut per divicias suas vitam eternam mereantur, et consolentur se pauperes invicem de eternis diviciis. Divites autem non spem ponant in diviciis huius mundi, que ad horam transeunt cum ipsis simul qui possident eas, sed spem ponant in eternis diviciis, ubi verum et eternum thesaurum inveniemus, christum filium dei, dominum nostrum, qui dedit nobis vitam et substantiam. Illi eidem domino nostro committo corpus et animam vestram. amen.
chunks.english:
We ought to explain to you why the Church has been accustomed to celebrate this week, more than other weeks of the year, with a greater practice of almsgiving.

This was established by the holy people who came before us, and by our ancestors, holy men who loved God with their whole heart. It seemed good to them that, after the gathering of the harvest, we should share some of it with the poor, in memory of the living and the dead and of our ancestors, and for the praise and glory of God, who bestowed these things on us.

For this reason it is commonly called the Common Week: so that everyone may celebrate this week together with every kind of good work, each person according to his means. In this way God may preserve and protect what he has given from fire, from robbers, and from every harmful attack.

Those to whom God has given the goods of this world should share with those who do not have them. For from the person to whom God has given more, he also requires more.

Let the poorer people pray to God for the rich, so that through their riches the rich may deserve eternal life. And let the poor comfort one another with the hope of eternal riches.

But the rich should not put their hope in the riches of this world, which pass away in a moment, together with the people who possess them. Instead, they should put their hope in eternal riches. There we will find the true and eternal treasure: Christ, the Son of God, our Lord, who gave us life and possessions.

To that same Lord I entrust your body and soul. Amen.
chunks.notes: The printed forms “parciamur” and “parciantur” are difficult; they appear to mean sharing or setting aside goods for the poor, and are translated accordingly. “Illi eidem domino nostro” is syntactically awkward; translated as “To that same Lord.”

chunks.speaker: announcer
chunks.chapter_title: Priests Rebuked for Neglecting Their People
chunks.latin: XXI. [Admonitio ad sacerdotes (in margine)]
chunks.english: Sermon 21. [Admonition to priests (note in the margin)]
chunks.notes: The marginal heading “Admonitio ad sacerdotes” means “Admonition to Priests.” The chapter title has been made descriptive for audio navigation.

chunks.speaker: narrator
chunks.latin: Apostolus clamat: Nomen dei plasphematur per vos. Nos sacerdotes, qui deberemus populum dei predicare verbis et exemplis, et deberemus eum iusticiam dei docere, et debemus imperitos ducere sicut videntes cecum; Heu nos ipsi ceci sumus ab omni iusticia et omni veritate, et utrique, tam nos duces quam ipsi sequentes, in foveam cadimus. Que est hec fovea? Potestas diaboli. Unde dicit beatus gregorius: Sacerdotes mali ruina sunt populi. Unde et propheta clamat: Ve sacerdotibus qui pascunt se ipsos bonis exterioribus, et populum dei negligunt in bonis spiritalibus. Et rursum clamat propheta: Sanguinem mei, videlicet peccata, de manibus vestris requiram. Vere nomen dei per vos plasphematur, quia quod nos prohibemus aliis, nos ipsi committimus: nos predicamus castitatem, et ipsi casti non sumus. Nos predicamus continentiam, et ipsi incontinentes sumus. Nos predicamus ieiunium, et ipsi non ieiunamus. Nos prohibemus avariciam, et ipsi avari sumus. Omne quod detestamur in aliis, hoc ipsi perpetramus. Quod ipse quoque apostolus expavescens dicit: Ne cum aliis predicatio, ipse reprobus efficiar. Homines ministrant nobis bona exteriora et pascunt corpus nostrum; nos deberemus animas eorum pascere epulis spiritalibus, videlicet predicatione divine iusticie et veritatis. Nos gloriam querimus, non gloriam dei. Nos gloriamur ex potestate et diviciis nostris, et non cogitamus quid commissum sit. Nos comedimus bona populi, et non laboramus quomodo animas eorum deo lucrifaciamus. Vere dico vobis, quia deus exigit a nobis omnes animas illas que ex nostra negligentia pereunt. Nos nulla caritate, nulla dulcedine regimus populum dei, sed cum quadam austeritate et indignatione magis provocamus eos ad iram et ad murmura contra nos. Immo exhortari debemus eos blandis ammonitionibus, et deberemus eos adtrahere cum omnimoda caritate, ut et nos ipsi simul cum eis conservaremur ad eternam vitam, Ut diceretur nobis a domino: Serve bone et fidelis, quia super pauca fuisti, videlicet in his terrenis, super multa te constituam, videlicet eternam vitam tibi dabo. Nobis non dicitur ab episcopo: Accipite divicias et utimini sicut vultis; sed dicitur nobis: accipite curam animarum, de quibus rationem reddituri estis in die iudicii. Hoc nobis valde timendum est. Hoc nobis valde terribile est. Non est professio aliqua super terram que deo gratius posset servire quam nos sacerdotes, quia et nos ipsos et alios possemus servare. Quia quoque aliquis nostrum plus diligit illum servum suum qui .x. vel .xx. vel plures manipulos affert ad horreum suum, quam illum qui tantum unum affert, hoc est qui se tantum servat. Ideo petro a domino: Si diligis me, pase oves meas, pascuis scilicet spiritualibus. Nos deberemus esse intercessores hominum ad deum omnipotentem, et deberemus esse mediatores inter deum et homines. Sed quomodo possumus intercedere pro eis, cum nos ipsi deum offendissemus et careamus gratia eius?
chunks.english:
The apostle cries out, “The name of God is blasphemed because of you.”

We priests ought to preach to the people of God by words and by example. We ought to teach them the justice of God. We ought to guide the unlearned as sighted people guide the blind. But alas, we ourselves are blind to all justice and all truth. And both groups together, we who lead and they who follow, fall into the ditch.

What is this ditch? It is the power of the devil.

For this reason blessed Gregory says, “Bad priests are the ruin of the people.” And so the prophet cries out, “Woe to the priests who feed themselves with outward goods, while neglecting the people of God in spiritual goods.” And again the prophet cries, “Their blood, that is, their sins, I will require from your hands.”

Truly, the name of God is blasphemed because of you. For the very things we forbid others to do, we do ourselves. We preach chastity, and we ourselves are not chaste. We preach self-control, and we ourselves are uncontrolled. We preach fasting, and we ourselves do not fast. We forbid greed, and we ourselves are greedy. Everything we condemn in others, we ourselves commit.

The apostle himself trembles at this when he says, “May it not happen that, after preaching to others, I myself should become rejected.”

People provide us with outward goods and feed our bodies. We ought to feed their souls with spiritual food: that is, with the preaching of divine justice and truth.

We seek our own glory, not the glory of God. We boast in our power and in our riches, and we do not consider what has been entrusted to us. We consume the goods of the people, but we do not labor to win their souls for God.

I tell you the truth: God will require from us all those souls that perish through our negligence.

We do not govern the people of God with charity or gentleness. Instead, with a kind of harshness and resentment, we provoke them all the more to anger and complaint against us. Rather, we ought to encourage them with gentle admonitions, and draw them in with every kind of charity, so that we ourselves, together with them, may be preserved for eternal life.

Then the Lord could say to us, “Good and faithful servant, because you have been faithful over a few things,” that is, over these earthly things, “I will set you over many things,” that is, I will give you eternal life.
